Correctness evidence

Copilot's observeActivity retains session.idle, abort, and
session.fusion_completed as real idle endpoints; assistant.turn_end no longer
publishes idle. It keeps foreground/sub-agent filtering, serialized posts,
failure reporting, and bounded shutdown idle repair. Root turn_end still
feeds the independent delivery-completion observation path.

OMP/Pi retains agent_end without willContinue and bounded shutdown idle
repair. turn_end still performs its local session bookkeeping and boundary
resend work; it no longer posts daemon idle. agent_end(true) stays working.

Consumers inspected: status badges; idle_nudge and its indexed own-event
anchor; PA idle-edge and presence/dormancy/size refresh; modal stall;
cold_wake; compaction wake; pointer worker idle-settle; background event
batch delivery; native extension lease renewal; queued-send turn-wait notes;
anomaly activity observations. These consume real busy/idle state or explicit
own-work events, not a required stream of tool-boundary idle pulses.

memory_turn::run uses its existing one task and subscription, filtered to
the target seat and future events. Own memory.note ends the wait, including
before prompt delivery has settled; it is not correlated to a prompt ID.
Historical/replayed notes and other seats' notes are not subscribed.
After the prompt's own delivered outcome, idle arms a settle deadline,
working clears it, and later idle starts a new deadline. Each timeout is
the minimum of settle and the original hold deadline. One loop termination
feeds one proceed call; the pending-seat guard and existing incarnation,
authority, and compare-and-set checks remain.

The turn-end reading is POLICY. Settle is a one-directional BRAKE: removing
it makes close/compact happen sooner, never later. Grace is AUTHORIZATION,
not a brake.

Security grace assessment

Source inspection confirms grace is issued only after this seat's held
close actually lands, not after compact or a skipped/failed close. Lookup
checks the cached pane, matching asserted IDs, monotonic expiry, recorded
process liveness and equal process start. Only parsed memory-add can use
this exceptional identity. Different pane/ID, recycled PID with a different
start, another valid verb, and expiry are refused by source-level guards.
Only the successful post-close write is exercised by the new integration
test; its other-verb example is unsupported syntax, so the valid-other-verb
guarantee is source inspection, not that assertion.

Known limit: the memory writer does not restrict a note to roles the author
held. That was already true for a live author in the unchanged
community/directory.rs:943-974 and community/memory.rs:177-180. Grace extends
the lifetime of memory-add authorization after close, not its role-target
privileges. Do not claim a held-role allowlist exists.

C34 follow-up, nonblocking: http/directory.rs:572-586 tries grace after any
normal identity refusal. http/identity.rs:1513-1524 can refuse a stale A
claim when the pane now belongs to B; http/memory_turn.rs:422-436 does not
recheck current live pane ownership. OMP /new can replace A with B in the
same still-live process, but successful boot updates PIJ_SESSION_ID to B;
an already-running CLI retaining A may legitimately be A's final note.
The focused security review therefore withdrew its initial MEDIUM
misattribution claim: no normal-use B-as-A write was established, and C33
does not make deliberate same-user impersonation a new vulnerability.
A rollover/grace regression could clarify the intended treatment of an
in-flight A note. No block for speculative hardening or missing fixtures.

The other requested note guarantee is also bounded: memory.note is fresh,
target-seat-scoped, and durable before publication, but not prompt-ID
correlated or required to follow delivered outcome. Accepting a fresh own
note before admission settles is intentional and explicitly unit-tested.
